scope: The exterior of the Canadian Museum for Human Rights in Winnipeg as documented in April 2014, with the limestone roots and northern galleries, curved glazed Cloud and 100-metre Tower of Hope.

references.filename: Canadian Museum for Human Rights, April 2014, showing sign with expected opening date.jpg

originalReview.notes: Northern aspect from Provencher Boulevard. Pale limestone masses step back toward the glass tower; the image shows the dark slots and long upper stone fins. The temporary opening sign is outside the building model.

references.filename: Canadian Museum for Human Rights, October 2012.JPG

originalReview.notes: October 2012 view from the southeast. The image controls the curved layered glass exterior, its dark recessed seam and the tower. Foreground equipment and site work are outside the building model.

quallaSearch.notes: Both exact Qualla files match the original self-released CC0 files. Wikimedia identifies Ccyyrree as a redirect to the same author’s current account, ElatedCoder. The 2014 photograph controls the stone face and represents the date. The earlier 2012 photograph controls the already recognizable Cloud and tower forms.
